question: Is there a storm coming this week?
html:
No storm is showing in our latest weather data

No. The latest snapshot shows no active National Weather Service alerts anywhere in our footprint, and the forecast shows dry, overcast days with no rain or snow. That data is from Nov 9, 2026, though, and the visible forecast only runs through Nov 11, so the rest of this week still needs a fresh check.

What the alerts show

  • Active alerts were zero in PA, NJ, MA, CT, RI, NH, ME and VT (National Weather Service alerts, Nov 9, 2026).
  • No winter storm, wind or flood warnings were in effect for any state we serve.

What the forecast shows

Six of our ten hubs are visible in the snapshot. All six show 0.0 inches of rain and snow every day from Nov 7 through Nov 11, overcast skies, and rain chances of 15% or lower (Open-Meteo 7-day forecast).

What a quiet week means

  • Our demand model raises expected calls only when a weather driver is active for a trade that day (Punctual Pros demand model).

A calm week with no weather surge is a chance to fill the schedule with tune-ups and planned work, and to staff for steady heating demand instead of holding crews back for emergencies.

Next actions

  • Re-pull the alerts and the 7-day forecast tonight. Confirm Nov 12 through Nov 18 for all ten hubs, including Beachwood.
  • Compare this week's booked calls in ServiceTitan with the model's November baseline. This gives a clean, weather-free calibration point.
  • Push heating tune-up outreach in high oil- and propane-heat counties such as Perry, Lebanon and Berks while crews have capacity (Punctual Pros market profile).
  • Set an alert trigger so dispatch is notified the moment any NWS warning appears in PA or NJ.
